critical_code_review_comments: DashboardLayout only filters sidebar NAV by permission; it does NOT redirect operator away from forbidden routes. Playwright test observed /channels URL remains /channels (empty content area). Backend returns 403 so no data leak, but UX should redirect to '/' when a route lacks hasPerm. Spec explicitly says 'navigating to /channels redirects to /' — this is a functional miss.

AlertBell is gated on `user?.role === 'admin'` only. Operators with 'channels.manage' or alert-related perms will never see alerts even if logically appropriate; current spec requires operators to have no bell which is fine, but tying it to role rather than perm is brittle.

/api/notify/test uses raw bot token in URL path (string formatting). Low risk since it's an admin-only test endpoint, but logging frameworks may capture the full URL. Consider stripping/masking in logs.
server.py is now 2120 lines; splitting into routers (reports, notify, accounts, operator) is overdue.

rca of the issue: Minor spec miss: operator navigating directly to /channels is not redirected to '/'; sidebar hides the link correctly and backend blocks the API (403), so there is no data leakage but the empty page is a UX bug.
